Solanum incanum Ruiz & Pav.[2]  
Solanum albidum is a species of nightshade native to western South America, ranging from southern Ecuador to northern Argentina, and thrives at mid elevations in the Andes. It is known by common names such as lumo (in Ecuador), huaritar (in Peru), and lavaplato plateado (in Bolivia). The plant can grow as either a shrub or a small tree. Its berries are dull yellow and measure 0.8–1.5 cm (0.31–0.59 in) in diameter.[2]
